title: Error handling and silent failure review
summary: Find swallowed errors, misleading fallbacks and lost context: every failure must be handled, propagated or recorded, and a fallback must never disguise a failure as success.

provenance.notes: Adds the rule that a default value returned on failure must be distinguishable from a real result.

outputs.name: findings
outputs.description: Each swallowed, mislabelled or context-losing failure with its location.

workflow.step: Search for empty catch blocks, ignored error returns, bare recover calls and broad except clauses.
workflow.check: Each match is classified handled, propagated, logged or swallowed.

workflow.step: For every fallback or default, ask whether a caller can tell it from a real result; if not, it hides failure.
Check that errors keep their cause and context when wrapped, and that logs include the operation and identifiers, never secrets.
workflow.check: A failure can be traced to its origin from the message.

workflow.step: Check retry and timeout logic for bounds, backoff and idempotency; an unbounded retry is a finding.
Check cleanup on failure paths: resources released, partial writes rolled back, state not left half-updated.
workflow.check: Error paths are as tested as success paths.

constraints: Read-only unless the task allows edits; never remove a failure signal to make a test pass.
Distinguish expected, recoverable errors from bugs.
Findings must cite the line that swallows or masks the error.

examples.title: Default on failure
examples.situation: A loader returns an empty config when parsing fails.
examples.guidance: Report it: the caller cannot tell empty from broken. Return the error or a typed unavailable result.

verification: Each finding has a path and a line.
Proposed fixes keep failures observable to the caller.

task.text: Hunt for a swallowed error and a silent failure behind the fallback in the loader.
The retry has no timeout and the catch hides the cause.
